-96.84090,33.10220.name: Dallas IVF
-96.84090,33.10220.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Brian D. Barnett, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

140.88977,38.22643.name: たんぽぽレディースクリニック
140.88977,38.22643.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-80.07579,40.39166.name: Altasciences Preclinical Scranton, Inc.
-80.07579,40.39166.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

0.12951,52.19715.name: Avenues Cambridge
0.12951,52.19715.state: 19E, Gillvray Health, Hills Road, Cambridge, CB2 1NW
0.12951,52.19715.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to Avenues. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-77.03000,38.90000.name: National Zoological Park
-77.03000,38.90000.type: Animal Welfare Act federal research facility
-77.03000,38.90000.desc: Federal research facility registered with USDA APHIS under the Animal Welfare Act, certificate 10-F-0010. This is the address on the registration. A research registration is issued to an organisation rather than to a building, so for a university it is usually the research administration office and the animals are elsewhere on campus or in another city. Rats, mice and birds bred for research are excluded from the Act's definition of an animal — the overwhelming majority of animals used, and the great majority of the genetically altered ones. What is covered here is dogs, cats, primates, rabbits, guinea pigs, hamsters and farm animals. The rest is counted nowhere.

-63.58373,44.63786.name: IWK Health Centre
-63.58373,44.63786.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, May 2025
-63.58373,44.63786.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, May 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-43.87584,-16.72447.name: Fertil ReproduÃ§Ã£o Humana
-43.87584,-16.72447.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://www.fertil.med.br/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere.

4.46792,51.91095.name: The Erasmus MC Complex
4.46792,51.91095.state: Doctor Molewaterplein 40, 3015 GD Rotterdam, The Netherlands, Netherlands
4.46792,51.91095.desc: A BSL3+ laboratory, operational. Run by Eramus. It is categorised as a public health laboratory, working on human health. It stands in a built-up area, with more than fifty thousand people living within two and a half miles. There is no international register of laboratories at this containment level and no obligation to declare one, so this record comes from a research project rather than a regulator. What that project could not find out is absent here too.

46.67530,24.71360.name: Saudi Food and Drug Authority — GM food rules
46.67530,24.71360.desc: Saudi Arabia requires labelling of engineered foods and approves specific events for import. A large food importer with mandatory labelling shapes what exporters are willing to ship, and does so without growing anything itself.

5.32000,60.39000.name: Mowi
5.32000,60.39000.desc: The largest farmed salmon producer in the world, Norwegian, operating across several countries. Escapes from farms of this scale have already introgressed into wild rivers with no engineering involved, which sets the baseline for any argument about engineered fish.

31.05000,-17.78300.name: La Vía Campesina
31.05000,-17.78300.desc: The largest farmers' organisation in the world, representing around 200 million smallholders across 81 countries, and the origin of the term food sovereignty. Its position on seed law rather than on biosafety is what makes it a principal here: it argues about who may save and replant, which is where UPOV bites.
